item.name: Exchange username and password for an access token

request.name: Exchange username and password for an access token

description.content:
Unknown user, wrong password, malformed username, and disabled account all return
the same 401 body. Password checks share a bounded pool (`HASH_MAX_CONCURRENT`);
when it is saturated the server answers 503 with `Retry-After` instead of queueing.
The 200 response is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

description.content:
Creates version 1 of the variable and advances the dictionary schema version by one.
`code`, `origin`, and `type` can never change afterwards.
Defaults: `origin` INPUT; `required` true for INPUT and false for DERIVED; `nullable` false;
`scale` 2 for DECIMAL. Amounts and bounds are decimal strings, never JSON numbers.
Ranges are sanity limits on the data, not credit policy: eligibility limits belong in RAC rules.

description.content:
Partial update. Omitted fields are unchanged, `null` clears `min_value` or `max_value`,
and an empty `unit` clears the unit. A change that alters something creates the next
version and advances the dictionary schema version; earlier versions stay readable via
`schema_version` on the list. Sending only values the variable already has changes
nothing: the response is the current version with no new version.
`code`, `origin`, and `type` are immutable and sending them is a 422. Variables are never deleted.
(Required)

request.name: Freeze a draft for approval

description.content:
Captures the canonical snapshot of the draft, including the data dictionary definitions
it was written against, stores its SHA-256 checksum, and moves the version to
`PENDING_APPROVAL`. After this nothing about the version changes: edits and a second
submit are 409 `POLICY_VERSION_FROZEN`. No request body.
Before freezing, the full policy validation of `POST .../validate` runs (SYSTEM_DESIGN.md
9.3): completeness (a scorecard, a decision matrix, and at least one required test case),
the RAC rules, the scorecard, the decision matrix against the scorecard range, and the test
cases, all against the dictionary version the draft is pinned to. If any check fails, the
answer is a 422 `POLICY_VALIDATION_FAILED` listing every problem (paths start with
`scorecard.` or `decision_matrix.` for those sections) and the draft stays a DRAFT.
Executing the test cases against the policy (comparing expected and actual decisions) is
a pending check until the decision evaluator exists (RF-011 to RF-013); approving or
rejecting a pending version arrives with M4.
(Required)

item.name: Replace the RAC rules of a draft

request.name: Replace the RAC rules of a draft

description.content:
Replaces the whole list in one step. The position in `rules` is the evaluation order, so
reordering is a PUT with the same rules in another order. An empty list removes all rules.
Nothing is stored unless every rule is valid, and every problem is reported together with
its path (`rules[2].expression`). Sending the list the draft already has changes nothing.

An `expression` is the condition an applicant must satisfy to **pass** the rule, written
in the `expr` language limited to: comparisons (`== != < <= > >=`), `and`/`or`/`not`
(also `&& || !`), arithmetic (`+ - * / %`), `in` / `not in` with a list of numbers or
booleans, number and boolean literals, `nil`, parentheses, and the names of data dictionary
variables. Function calls, strings, member access, conditionals, and everything else are
rejected (`unsupported_syntax`). The expression must be boolean and well typed against the
dictionary version the draft is pinned to (`dictionary_schema_version`). `action` says what
a failed rule does: `REJECT` ends the evaluation with a rejection, `REFER` sends the
application to manual review and scoring continues. Rules are only checked here, not run;
evaluation arrives with RF-012.

Issue codes for `expression`: `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_characters`, `syntax_error`,
`unsupported_syntax`, `unknown_variable`, `type_error`. `message` carries the explanation.
Only a DRAFT can change: any other status is a 409 `POLICY_VERSION_FROZEN`.
(Required)

item.name: Replace the scorecard of a draft

request.name: Replace the scorecard of a draft

description.content:
Replaces the whole scorecard in one step: `total_score = base_score + the points of the one
bin each characteristic selects` (SYSTEM_DESIGN.md 10.3). Characteristics keep the order
given, and each one scores one numeric data dictionary variable.

**Bins are half-open intervals `[min_value, max_value)`**: `min_value` is included,
`max_value` is not. An omitted or null `min_value` means no lower limit and an omitted or
null `max_value` means no upper limit. Bins are listed in ascending order and must cover
every value the variable can have exactly once: the first bin starts at or below the
variable's dictionary minimum (or has no `min_value`), each bin starts where the previous
one ends (`gap` / `overlap` otherwise), and the last bin ends above the dictionary maximum
(or has no `max_value`). So every valid input selects exactly one bin. Bounds follow the
variable type: whole numbers for INTEGER (`must_be_integer`), at most the variable's scale
for DECIMAL (`exceeds_scale`). They are returned in shortest form (`"0.30"` becomes `"0.3"`).

`base_score`, `points`, and `missing_points` are decimal strings with at most two decimals
(NUMERIC(12,2)); they are returned with exactly two and may be negative. Sums are exact.
`missing_points` is the explicit outcome when the variable is absent or null, and is only
allowed for an optional input variable (`variable_always_present` otherwise).

Everything is checked against the dictionary version the draft is pinned to. Nothing is
stored unless the whole scorecard is valid; every problem is reported with its path
(`characteristics[1].bins[2].min_value`). Sending the scorecard the draft already has
changes nothing. Only a DRAFT can change (409 `POLICY_VERSION_FROZEN`).
(Required)

item.name: Replace the decision matrix of a draft

request.name: Replace the decision matrix of a draft

description.content:
Replaces the whole matrix in one step. Each row maps a total score to a risk `grade` and a
`decision` (`APPROVE`, `REFER`, or `REJECT`; there is no default) (SYSTEM_DESIGN.md 10.4).

**Rows are half-open score intervals `[min_score, max_score)`**: `min_score` is included,
`max_score` is not, the same rule as scorecard bins. An omitted or null `min_score` means no
lower limit (first row only) and an omitted or null `max_score` no upper limit (last row
only). Rows are listed in ascending order and each starts where the previous one ends
(`gap` / `overlap` otherwise). When the draft has a scorecard, the rows must also cover
every total it can produce (`score_range`): the first row starts at or below its minimum
and the last ends above its maximum (`does_not_cover_score_range`). So no score of this
version can ever find no row. Bounds are decimal strings with at most two decimals and are
returned with exactly two. For the demo score domain 0 to 900 inclusive the last row ends
at `901`.

Nothing is stored unless the whole matrix is valid; every problem is reported with its path
(`rows[1].min_score`). Sending the matrix the draft already has changes nothing. At least
one row is required; remove a matrix with `DELETE`. Only a DRAFT can change (409
`POLICY_VERSION_FROZEN`). The matrix is checked, not run: lookup at decision time and the
precedence of RAC results over the matrix arrive with RF-013.

item.name: Replace the test cases of a draft

request.name: Replace the test cases of a draft

description.content:
Replaces the whole list. A test case is an applicant `input` (the same facts the decision
API will take: integers as JSON numbers, decimals as strings, booleans) and the result the
policy is expected to give: either a business `DECISION` (with `decision`, optional
`grade`, and optional `reason_codes`) or an `INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR`. Cases are `required`
unless set to false; a version can only be submitted with at least one required case.

Each case is checked now, against the dictionary version the draft is pinned to and the
draft's current RAC rules and decision matrix:
input keys must be input variables of the dictionary (`unknown_variable`,
`derived_not_allowed`); `grade` must be a grade of the matrix (`unknown_grade`) and every
reason code a reason code of a RAC rule (`unknown_reason_code`); and the input is **run
against the data dictionary**: a `DECISION` case needs an input that passes it (the issue
of the dictionary is reported at `input.<variable>`), and an `INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR` case
needs one that fails it (`validation_error_not_raised`). Whether the expected decision,
grade, and reason codes are what the policy gives is checked once the decision evaluator
exists (RF-011 to RF-013); `POST .../validate` lists that as a pending check.

Reason codes are a set and are returned sorted. Nothing is stored unless every case is
valid; every problem is reported with its path. Sending the list the draft already has
changes nothing; an empty list removes all cases. Only a DRAFT can change (409
`POLICY_VERSION_FROZEN`).
(Required)

request.name: Validate a whole policy version

description.content:
Runs the full policy validation of SYSTEM_DESIGN.md 9.3 and returns a report; nothing
changes. Submit runs the same checks and refuses the version (422
`POLICY_VALIDATION_FAILED`, same `issues`) when any fails, so this is the dry run of
submit and needs the same permission. Works for any status; a frozen version is checked
again against the dictionary version it is pinned to. No request body.

Checks: **completeness** (a scorecard, a decision matrix, and at least one required test
case: `missing_section`, `no_required_test_cases`; RAC rules are optional); every **RAC
expression** compiles and type-checks; the **scorecard** variables exist and are numeric
and its bins cover each variable exactly once; the **decision matrix** covers the
scorecard's score range; every **test case** references existing variables, grades, and
reason codes, and its input passes or fails the data dictionary as its expected outcome
says. Paths are those of the editing endpoints, prefixed `scorecard.` and
`decision_matrix.` for those sections.

`pending_checks` lists what cannot run yet: comparing each test case's expected decision,
grade, and reason codes with the policy's actual result needs the decision evaluator
(RF-011 to RF-013). `valid: true` therefore means "every check that exists passed", and
the pending check is always listed so it is never mistaken for a pass.
(Required)

Contract for the endpoints implemented so far (RF-001 to RF-010, plus M1 hardening).

- All `/api/v1` endpoints except login require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Authorization is permission-based. Each operation lists the required permission
  in `x-required-permission`; the role-to-permission matrix lives in
  `app/modules/identity/domain/permission.go`.
- Every response produced by the application carries an `X-Request-ID` header, and JSON
  error bodies repeat it as `request_id`. `408` and `413` are written by the HTTP driver
  and may not carry it.
- Semantic validation errors use HTTP 422 consistently.
- Request bodies are limited to 64 KiB. Requests are limited to 3 seconds.
- Optional gateway headers `X-App`, `X-Path-Gateway`, `X-Request-From`, `X-Request-User`,
  `X-Device-ID`, and `X-Request-Tags` are recorded in the server's activity log for tracing.
  They never affect authorization; `X-Request-User` is informational only.
- `408 Request Timeout` and `413 Payload Too Large` are written by the HTTP driver, so
  their body is plain text, not the JSON error envelope. A 408 means the client stopped
  waiting; the handler may still finish server-side, but its database work uses the
  request deadline and is cancelled.
  Unmatched routes (any method) return a JSON `404 ROUTE_NOT_FOUND`.
